display: SmoothEPD comes from a line of fast e-paper hacks. PaperBoy drove a raw parallel panel at 60 Hz. InkBoy got about 30 fps from a 1.54-inch SSD1681. SmoothEPD states 47 Hz on the same 200x200 panel.
spoken: Smooth E P D comes from a line of fast e-paper hacks. PaperBoy drove a raw parallel panel, at sixty hertz. InkBoy got about thirty frames a second from a one point five four inch, S S D sixteen eighty-one. Smooth E P D states forty-seven hertz, on the same two hundred by two hundred panel.

display: Those panels, and our 4.2-inch SSD1683, sit behind a controller. You send a picture, and it applies a fixed waveform to each old-to-new change. No per-pixel control.
spoken: Those panels, and our four point two inch S S D sixteen eighty-three, sit behind a controller. You send a picture, and it applies a fixed waveform to each old-to-new change. No per-pixel control.

display: The trick: the two RAM planes stop being pictures. One means drive black, the other drive white, with a one-frame LUT of about 20 ms. A pixel in neither plane holds.
spoken: The trick: the two RAM planes stop being pictures. One means, drive black. The other, drive white. With a one-frame lut, of about twenty milliseconds. A pixel in neither plane, holds.

display: Each pixel gets a budget of 7 scans, about 140 ms. The budget reloads whenever the pixel's target changes, even if it flips back halfway.
spoken: Each pixel gets a budget of seven scans, about a hundred and forty milliseconds. The budget reloads whenever the pixel's target changes, even if it flips back halfway.

display: Slowed down: a pixel goes black for 2 frames, then back to white. SmoothEPD drives it white right away, for the full 7. Our lag trick erases it late, with only 2 white frames.
spoken: Slowed down: a pixel goes black for two frames, then back to white. Smooth E P D drives it white right away, for the full seven. Our lag trick erases it late, with only two white frames.

display: Even a clean change is short for us: lag 6 times 8 ms is 48 ms of drive. Their budget is 140, above the 120 ms their README calls the minimum.
spoken: Even a clean change is short for us: lag six, times eight milliseconds, is forty-eight milliseconds of drive. Their budget is a hundred and forty, above the hundred and twenty their readme calls the minimum.

display: Their author also tried a net-balanced variant, where the erase only matches the on-time. He wrote that it trails heavily. That is our gray smear, and lag 6 or 8 did not fix it.
spoken: Their author also tried a net-balanced variant, where the erasing pulse only matches the on-time. He wrote that it trails heavily. That is our gray smear, and lag six or eight did not fix it.

display: The price: full drive both ways is not DC balanced. So every pixel keeps a debt count. Every 1000 scans it pays back one unit, only toward the color it already shows.
spoken: The price: full drive both ways is not D C balanced. So every pixel keeps a debt count. Every thousand scans, it pays back one unit, only toward the color it already shows.

display: The real reset is a balanced full refresh: 66 frames, 1.3 s, every 2000 scans, about every 43 s. Ours is a 3.3 s OTP clean every 15 s.
spoken: The real reset is a balanced full refresh: sixty-six frames, one point three seconds, every two thousand scans. About every forty-three seconds. Ours is a three point three second O T P clean, every fifteen seconds.

display: Their demos are drawn to suit the panel: thick strokes, motion of one pixel per frame, digits that change every 7 frames, and slow physics.
spoken: Their demo programs are drawn to suit the panel: thick strokes, motion of one pixel per frame, digits that change every seven frames, and slow physics.

display: What we will try, in order: budget masks for the teapot, computed on the Mac. Lag 15 as a control. Their balanced refresh LUT. A same-color settle. A coarser dither. Faster SPI.
spoken: What we will try, in order: budget masks for the teapot, computed on the Mac. Lag fifteen, as a control. Their balanced refresh lut. A same-color settle. A coarser dither. And faster S P I.

display: Caveats: 47 Hz is the author's own claim; nobody else has measured it. Breaking DC balance needs Mikey's OK. And panel lifetime under any of this is unknown.
spoken: Caveats: forty-seven hertz is the author's own claim; nobody else has measured it. Breaking D C balance needs Mikey's OK. And panel lifetime, under any of this, is unknown.
